Here is Section 1 of your Form I-9, filled in from what you gave me. Five things are still yours to fill in: your US address, your email, your signature, the date, and the I-94 number if you'd rather use that.

Section 1. Employee Information and Attestation

[B01] Last Name (Family Name): SURNAME_P1
[B02] First Name (Given Name): GIVEN_P1
[B03] Middle Initial (if any): MIDDLE_P1
      By hand: this box takes only your middle initial. Once your name is back in place, keep just the first letter of your middle name and delete the rest.
[B04] Other Last Names Used (if any): N/A
[B05] Address (Street Number and Name): NEEDS-YOU
[B06] Apt. Number (if any): NEEDS-YOU
[B07] City or Town: NEEDS-YOU
[B08] State: NEEDS-YOU
[B09] ZIP Code: NEEDS-YOU
      Missing: your new US address (street, apartment if any, city, state, ZIP). mdoc doesn't have it. ADDRESS_P1 is your saved home address, and the I-9 wants the place you live in the US now, so I left it out. Write the US address in these five boxes yourself. Don't put a PO box here.
[B10] Date of Birth (mm/dd/yyyy): DATE_P1
      By hand: this alias is your birth date in your passport's format. Rewrite it as mm/dd/yyyy: two-digit month, two-digit day, four-digit year.
[B11] U.S. Social Security Number: leave blank
      You don't have a number yet, and you shouldn't make one up or write "applied for". Tell your employer you've applied (or will apply). If they use E-Verify, they'll wait to open your case until your number arrives, then add it.
[B12] Employee's Email Address: NEEDS-YOU (optional)
      Missing: your email address. This box is optional, so you can leave it blank. If you add one, DHS may use it to contact you about E-Verify.
[B13] Employee's Telephone Number: PHONE_P1
      Optional. If PHONE_P1 is a Philippine number and you'll have a US number soon, you can write the US number by hand or leave the box blank.

Citizenship or immigration status:
[B14] [ ] 1. A citizen of the United States
      [ ] 2. A noncitizen national of the United States
      [ ] 3. A lawful permanent resident
      [X] 4. An alien authorized to work until (exp. date, if any): 09/30/2029

[B15] USCIS A-Number: (leave blank)
      OR Form I-94 Admission Number: (leave blank)
      OR Foreign Passport Number and Country of Issuance: ID_P1, Philippines
      Fill in only one of the three. Most H-1B workers don't have an A-Number, so I used your passport. Your I-94 Admission Number works too, but mdoc doesn't have it. If you'd rather use it, write the 11-character number from your I-94 record and leave the passport line blank.

[B16] Signature of Employee: NEEDS-YOU
      You must sign this yourself, on paper or electronically if your employer's system offers it.
[B17] Today's Date (mm/dd/yyyy): NEEDS-YOU
      Write the date you sign, as mm/dd/yyyy. Section 1 must be finished by your first day of work (next Monday) at the latest. It can't be done before you accepted the job offer.

Preparer and/or Translator Certification: you only need this page if someone helps you fill in Section 1. If you complete it yourself, check the box saying you used no preparer or translator.

Before you sign, check these:
- Make sure 09/30/2029 matches the "Admit Until" date on your I-94 record (and your I-797 approval notice). If the I-94 shows a different date, use the I-94 date in box 4.
- For Section 2, your employer will need to see original documents within three business days of your start date. For an H-1B worker, the usual choice from List A is your Philippine passport together with your Form I-94. Bring both. You can print your I-94 from the CBP I-94 website.
- Your place of birth, your passport's issue date and its issuing authority don't go on Section 1. I didn't use them.
